outcome: WON on attempt 1, 5 turns, 1 player faint

attempts.note: Weavile fainted to Venonat's Struggle Bug (Bug is 2x on Dark). Whimsicott reached 14/45. Arcanine's Flare Blitz is 2x on all four members and decided the fight.

strategy_checks.check: Venonat's Rage Powder protects the setup partner
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 1: Rage Powder selected (flinched by my faster Fake Out). Turn 4: Rage Powder resolved and pulled Arcanine's Flare Blitz off Kricketune onto Venonat, which died taking it. That is the intended sacrifice and it saved the Focus Sash finisher from a 2x hit.

strategy_checks.check: Grass-type powder immunity bypasses Rage Powder
strategy_checks.evidence: On the same turn 4, Whimsicott (Grass/Fairy) was NOT redirected - its Moonblast resolved against Kricketune (battler 1) while Arcanine's attack was pulled to battler 3. The authored crack ('powder immunity bypasses Venonat') works exactly as documented.

strategy_checks.check: Beautifly gets a safe Quiver Dance behind the powder
strategy_checks.evidence: Beautifly chose Bug Buzz on turn 1, was withdrawn on turn 2 at 24/52, returned on turn 4 and chose Bug Buzz again on turn 5 before fainting. Quiver Dance was never selected in either appearance, including turn 1 when its partner had already committed to Rage Powder - the exact board the plan describes.

strategy_checks.check: Dustox supplies the alternate Tailwind window
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 3 chosen action: battler 1 MOVE_TAILWIND. Arcanine's Flare Blitz (2x) killed Dustox before it moved. The choice was correct; execution was denied by speed, not by the AI.

strategy_checks.check: Kricketune's Fell Stinger earns the Attack boost only on a genuine knockout
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 4: Fell Stinger hit Whimsicott and did not KO it (Whimsicott ended at 14/45). No Attack boost was applied, which matches the authored rule that an ordinary hit does not earn it.

strategy_checks.check: Venonat's Compound Eyes Sleep Powder lands a sleep
strategy_checks.evidence: Venonat had Compound Eyes (100% accurate Sleep Powder) and was on the field for four turns. It chose Rage Powder, Struggle Bug, Protect and Rage Powder. Sleeping Arcanine on turn 3 or 4 was the strongest available action and was never considered.
Kricketune chose Fell Stinger and Protect in its two acting turns; Taunt never appeared against an active Prankster Whimsicott.

protect_ledger.payoff: MINOR REAL - blocked Whimsicott's Moonblast, which was only 0.5x into Bug/Poison. It cost Venonat a turn to prevent roughly a tenth of its HP while its partner Dustox died to the Flare Blitz it did not redirect.
EMPTY - Arcanine's Flare Blitz went to Beautifly and Whimsicott spent the turn switching out, so the guard blocked nothing.

ai_observations: The SETUP half of this trainer's four strategy flags (SETUP, TAILWIND, REDIRECTION, PRESSURE) never executed: Beautifly declined Quiver Dance in both of its appearances. REDIRECTION executed perfectly, TAILWIND was chosen but outsped, PRESSURE is ambient.

Venonat's Sleep Powder plus Compound Eyes is the single strongest tool on this team and was never selected across four turns on the field. Worth a focused look at how the scorer prices a guaranteed sleep against a healthy attacker.
Venonat's turn-3 Protect is the weakest guard in the fight: it guarded against a resisted special attack and spent the turn its partner needed a redirect.

level_changes.reason: Brief rule 5: won first try with 1 player faint -> +1 to the weakest member. Beautifly is the only member below offset 4 (level 14 against Venonat/Dustox/Kricketune at 16) and it is also the member whose authored job, Quiver Dance, never happened. The other three are already two levels above cap and were left alone.

cooler_note: The concept is good and the redirection half of it genuinely showed up in play, which is rare in this block. The problem is that a four-member mono-Bug team loses to one Fire attacker: Arcanine's Flare Blitz is 2x on Beautifly, Venonat, Dustox and Kricketune alike, so the whole room has a single answer. Suggestion for a later pass, not applied here: swap Dustox (the most redundant slot - a second Bug/Poison whose Tailwind never resolves because it is slower than the threats it wants to outrun) for a partner that punishes the Fire answer, so the powder support is protecting something the player cannot simply burn through. Keep Venonat and Kricketune exactly as they are; the powder-and-finisher pairing is the interesting idea here.
not_finished: Quiver Dance, Sleep Powder, Taunt and a resolved Tailwind are all still unexercised. The +1 has not been retested in a rebuilt ROM.
